title: Set Operations and Division in Relational Algebra

blocks.text: Imagine you have two lists of students enrolled in different courses. How can you find students enrolled in both courses, only one course, or all courses combined? Relational algebra set operations provide the tools to answer these questions.

blocks.markdown: In relational algebra, set operations allow us to manipulate and query relational data by treating relations as mathematical sets. The primary set operations are **union**, **intersection**, and **difference**. These operations require the relations to be **union-compatible**.

blocks.title: Union Compatibility
blocks.text: Two relations are union-compatible if they have the same number of attributes and corresponding attributes have the same domain.

blocks.markdown: Let's explore each of these set operations with formal definitions and examples.

blocks.title: Union Example
blocks.prompt: Given relations R and S, find R ∪ S.

steps.text: R ∪ S includes all tuples from both R and S without duplication.

blocks.latex: R \cap S = \{ t \mid t \in R \text{ and } t \in S \}
blocks.caption: Intersection of two relations R and S.

blocks.title: Intersection Example
blocks.prompt: Find the intersection of relations R and S.

steps.text: Using the same R = \{(1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob')\} and S = \{(2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Charlie')\}, find common tuples.
Identify tuples present in both R and S.

blocks.caption: Difference of two relations R and S.

steps.text: Using R = \{(1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob')\} and S = \{(2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Charlie')\}, find tuples in R not in S.
Identify tuples in R that are not in S.
The tuple (1, 'Alice') is only in R.

blocks.markdown: Another powerful operation in relational algebra is **division**, which is used to express 'for all' queries. It is useful when you want to find tuples in one relation that are related to all tuples in another relation.

blocks.title: Division in Relational Algebra
blocks.text: Division is used to find tuples in one relation that are associated with all tuples in another relation.

rows: Finds common tuples in two relations.
Finds tuples in one relation not in another.
Finds tuples related to all tuples in another relation.
